guides.opening: Welcome back. You already carry something real into this chemistry course: your work on osmosis and diffusion gave you a solid grip on concentration — the idea that particles move from crowded to less crowded places. We will start there and build outward. You also studied how enzymes speed up reactions in cells; that same logic of factors controlling reaction speed is exactly the move we use in reaction rates. From concentration we will reach into atomic structure, chemical bonding, and acids and bases. Nothing here starts from zero for you — it starts from what you already know.
guides.self_check: No food or diet examples appear anywhere in the opening text.

guides.opening: Welcome to biochemistry. You are better prepared than you might think. From cell biology, you already understand enzymes — we will now go deeper into how they work, examining the rates and rules that govern their action. From intro chemistry, your grasp of reaction rates gives you the exact foundation enzyme kinetics is built on. Your chemical-bonding knowledge, together with the functional groups you studied in organic chemistry, directly opens up protein structure. Those threads — enzymes, rates, bonding, functional groups — weave together here into metabolism and molecular mechanism. No new starting point needed; we pick up exactly where you left off.
guides.self_check: Opening contains no food or diet examples, no 3-D spinning molecule visuals, and no mention of mitosis.

guides.opening: Welcome back — it has been about six months, so let us ease in gently rather than assuming everything is fresh. You have real foundations to build on here: your chemical-bonding work from intro-chemistry connects directly to how we will explore DNA structure, and your protein-structure knowledge from biochemistry is exactly where translation picks up. Molecular biology is the story of how cells read their own instructions — and you already hold key chapters. We will review the bridges before pushing forward, so nothing feels dropped in from nowhere. Ready to see how your earlier work opens the door to this one?
